# Cognition Therapeutics Announces CTAD Poster Highlighting Screening Efficiencies with p-Tau217 in the Ongoing Phase 2 START Study


November 17, 2026 06:00 ET


*– Efficient screening processes may reduce participant and site burden in clinical trials –*


PURCHASE, N.Y., Nov. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) —[Cognition Therapeutics, Inc.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=Vfiiap9Pmd-BQdkbdp2x1SInUrDd9gBrQ_vZbtvYLl9_1yYI_5Uh02Or0T5QZjh5iy3Lmf-seaAnSQZkC7uDOyl6yc0q5eNwg_K5d_aOFOSyxsSiUzhphHheBNQR8lGJ) , (the Company or Cognition) (NASDAQ: CGTX), a clinical-stage company developing drugs that treat neurodegenerative disorders, announced that our partners at the Alzheimer’s Clinical Trials Consortium (ACTC) are presenting an Alzheimer’s disease screening strategy that may reduce the burden on participants and clinical sites. The poster will be presented at the annual Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) conference being held November 16-19 in Boston, MA. The analysis was led by Cognition’s collaborators at ACTC, a clinical trial network of 32 leading academic sites with expertise in clinical trials in Alzheimer’s disease funded by the National Institute of Aging (NIA), a part of the National Institutes of Health (grant number U24AG057437).


Insights presented at CTAD are drawn from Cognition’s Phase 2 START study (COG0203,[NCT05531656](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=N08PHy8_sMQh7DIuOX61PWl4cIYZSja18x8Lqm6LckRhNOs1C1PAujvBDsvlmPQPNcO1FWinqnlX8OZKvkhhuN4j3kS9RRzqOo2cEiOC3WMt7_7cS4Vmklb2r1-RBZ5G) ), which was among the first trials of an early Alzheimer’s therapeutic to incorporate the measurement of plasma p-tau217 at the time of initial screening. P-tau217 is a protein that has emerged as an indicator of Alzheimer’s disease pathology. By using a blood test to measure p-tau217 during screening, the clinical trial staff were able to exclude people who were ineligible to participate before confirmation with amyloid PET.


“PET scans can assess the presence of amyloid in the brain consistent with Alzheimer’s disease,” explained Marina Ritchie, Ph.D., a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Southern California’s Epstein Family Alzheimer’s Therapeutic Research Institute and lead author on the CTAD poster. “Imaging techniques, however, are often costly, resource intensive, and can add burden to participants and trial sites. As a less invasive and more scalable screening tool, early incorporation of plasma biomarkers into the trial screening process may help identify individuals unlikely to meet biomarker eligibility criteria and reduce unnecessary screening visits for participants.”


[The START study](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=ad8wjCkOz9kXo9lEfAUW00tZru8nemV2_69UD2kSQ9Yhn4Zw6IA9LjDYMMmCl2I-iMvBFewSXtPeC4sTlPke1rtAeuFdw_tX4Gius-Dnfeo=) is evaluating once-daily oral zervimesine (CT1812) or placebo in 545 individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or early Alzheimer’s disease. Cognition is conducting the START study in collaboration with ACTC, with major grant support from NIA (grant number R01AG065248). Enrollment in START was completed in the fourth quarter of 2025, and top-line results are expected after the last participants have completed 18 months of treatment.


“We believe that we can set future trials apart by designing them with the needs of participants, care partners and sites in mind, starting with efficient screening practices,” added[Anthony Caggiano, M.D., Ph.D.,](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=O2kDd7waRpoWhzRU7itQzYxAISvFXN7wXGo1Anu0ql43cucr_bsM3GABZwcI5Nn3bR467doUXcLNVMyPG8ZLhhF5bcKXJfS18zrqNvLFfhrHkFBP8AYgikkuCgxFyK3zlDVUoeLQ4fqIG7gOmqlKtg==) Cognition’s chief medical officer. “Reducing the need for imaging allows sites to complete screening visits in less time with fewer resources.”


The CTAD poster will be available on the[Publications](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=qVBHF-KRxD00sVExevjdwis4tlEuuwOTOssgadtLmoDxeeJOeWnHwQ7Q5aXMssfYHqPdrResWJc6leyd9v1_sacZt2PCvpM9ML_WuIrvNZw=) page of the company website in accordance with the conference embargo policy.


**CTAD Presentation Details:**
Conference: November 16–19, 2026 in Boston, MA
Poster Session: November 19, 2026 in the Gloucester Room
Poster Title: Plasma p-tau217 In Early Alzheimer’s Disease Trial Screening: Insights from START
Authors: Ritchie M, Langford O, Liang Y, Burns D, Flournoy C, Grill JD, Caggiano A, Grundman M, Rissman RA, Aisen P, van Dyck CH, Raman R


**About Cognition Therapeutics**
[Cognition Therapeutics, Inc.](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=Vfiiap9Pmd-BQdkbdp2x1SInUrDd9gBrQ_vZbtvYLl_neEkpbRKDTXpF2h2jjV-fkqxTgGFw8u_1nsigA9i3oBtd7VKkTPkaxPYsETRCjO8sp80-BL-9wwMtzaD8t5il) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to helping millions of families seeking effective treatments for devastating neurodegenerative diseases through the development of novel, accessible therapies. The company has led pioneering research into the underlying mechanisms of degenerative nerve disorders. Our scientific approach builds on well-established biological pathways and translates across indications in which toxic oligomers drive disease progression, offering potential in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), Alzheimer’s disease, geographic atrophy, Parkinson’s, among others. Backed by nearly $200 million in National Institutes of Health and related foundation grants, Cognition Therapeutics continues to advance clinical research in its efforts to bring forth solutions that meet patients where they are and reduce caregiver burden. **About Zervimesine (CT1812)**
The company’s lead candidate, zervimesine (CT1812), is an investigational once-daily oral therapy that has demonstrated promise in Phase 2 clinical trials in DLB and mild-to-moderate Alzheimer’s disease.[Zervimesine](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=Oq9ENrkaOm058gpmb0leHau3WGRNWAbJ9Lazk5sPepPDHjWlLH9tdIVtP8awT1mCmPrQfnQH0-ajz6kK-Uv9IJswmeq-3-LGwqAZ4fXfavI=) (CT1812) is currently being studied in the Phase 2 START Study ([NCT05531656](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=N08PHy8_sMQh7DIuOX61PZlWmnG3-cLyBViITwhUcaq5B5g0TXOMtgzkxeHlb6jvxgMhLYsZ6FxHlSeNo4p8_-2HOiidlqVg_araUPBK_mO2NKZU2q2TbI2zguhM8X1g) ) in patients with MCI and early Alzheimer’s disease. Phase 2 clinical studies have concluded in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), mild-to-moderate Alzheimer’s disease, and geographic atrophy secondary to dry AMD. Based in part on the strong efficacy signals observed in the Phase 2 SHIMMER study in DLB ([NCT05225415](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=N08PHy8_sMQh7DIuOX61PSckoB9nqnucBgPh9MncIqwNLZFpXbsocLzm8uwy180ZTj_Gjo-eGNhFpbL4S6f5-NwSlvK_s5OMeBY_e3oWSiGnVf5JUNhI3TLKuyTgMzAN) ), the company plans to advance zervimesine into a registrational trial for people with DLB who experience psychosis. Zervimesine has been generally well tolerated in clinical studies to date.


The USAN Council has adopted zervimesine as the United States Adopted Name (USAN) for CT1812.
